messages.author: 539623a2f30c9e53
messages.subject: Two questions about text
parts:
Hello all,

I'm sure there's a fairly simple answer to the first one, but I've been unable to find one in the book or the archives. I have a plot annotated with geom_text, but the font appears to be bold. Is there some way to change it to regular font weight?

My second questions is somewhat more obscure. I've been experimenting with using ggplot2 in combination with the tikzDevice package. However, tikzDevice seems to ignore the font size I specify in ggplot2. Does anybody happen to know how to fix this?

Thanks,

Jonathan Christensen

messages.author: 539623a2f30c9e53
messages.subject: Re: Two questions about text
parts:
Hello again,

I figured the first one out (the text was regular font weight, but was written over itself several times, giving it the appearance of being bold), but the second is still up in the air. From what I understand, tikzDevice is supposed to respect the cex parameter, at least applied to viewports. I tried using the cex parameter instead of size= in geom_text, but no luck. Does anybody here (I understand from previous posts that at least some of the list members use tikzDevice) happen to know how to change the font size of a geom_text annotation using ggplot and tikzDevice?

Thanks,

Jonathan Christensen

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Two questions about text
parts:
Hi,

it is my understanding that the size argument of ggplot2 geoms is
converted to the cex argument of grid graphics before rendering. So if
you specify the size with annotate() it should work, irrespective of
the device (otherwise it's a bug in the device).

HTH,

baptiste

messages.author: 539623a2f30c9e53
messages.subject: Re: Two questions about text
parts:
Baptiste,

Thanks for the help.

It looks to me like the size argument, at least for the text geom, is converted to a fontsize argument:

> GeomText$draw
proto method (instantiated with ): function (., data, scales, coordinates, ..., parse = FALSE)
{
    lab <- data$label
    if (parse) {
        lab <- parse(text = lab)
    }
    with(coordinates$transform(data, scales), textGrob(lab, x,
        y, default.units = "native", hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust,
        rot = angle, gp = gpar(col = alpha(colour, alpha), fontsize = size *
            .pt)))
}

Unfortunately, tikzDevice ignores fontsize. One of the authors says it's partly philosophical--the whole point of tikzDevice is to let LaTeX take care of all the fonts--and partly practical--it might be possible to convert the fontsize argument to a cex argument, but it would require significant changes to the code and he hasn't gotten around to doing it (and, as far as I understand, it isn't in his plans for the near future).

For now I've resorted to using text.grid to draw on top of the ggplot2 plot. It's a little bit of a hack, but it works for now. If anybody else comes up with a better way, please let me know.

Thanks again,
Jonathan

messages.author: cc640420b3a8b338
messages.subject: Re: Two questions about text
parts:
Hi,

From some of the help I've recevied on stackoverflow:

\begin{tikzpicture}[font=\scriptsize]
\draw (0,0) rectangle (1,1) -- +(-1,-1);
\node(text) at (0.5,0.5) {Text};
\end{tikzpicture}

or

or setting the option \tikzset{font=\scriptsize}

Do either of these work for you? You can for example genereate the
tikz file with the barebones option and then wrap then:
\begin{tikzpicture}[font=\scriptsize]
\input{my_graph}
\end{tikzpicture}

Another bit of help from stackoverflow on my first question yielded
the answer:
\begin{tikzpicture}

\tikzstyle{every node}=[font=\small]

\end{tikzpicture}

I'm still struggling with my case which is an issue with the scaling
of the images nad that effect on font size in tikzpictures.

Hope that helps.

Jay

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Two questions about text
parts:
Oops, I should have checked the code, I was lead by the mistaken
assumption that size was mapped to cex, not fontsize. I'm not sure I
understand the difference to be honest, what was the reason to prefer
fontsize over cex? It would be trivial to make a new geom, geom_text2
say, using cex instead but that'd be a bit of a kludge.
As much as I appreciate the great work put into the tikzDevice package
I don't understand the argument here, it seems to me that this is a
fairly important problem as opposed to a feature (it is my
understanding that devices should reproduce the intended output
without consideration of arbitrary aesthetic preferences).

Best,

baptiste
